Overweight Calculator

Compare adult BMI with the standard BMI 25 screening threshold and estimate the weight corresponding to that threshold for a given height. The output is a screening comparison and does not judge body composition or an individual’s health. BMI=weight(kg)/height(m)². The BMI-25 comparison weight is 25×height(m)²; the difference is shown only when current weight is above that reference. This is a screening threshold for adults, not a health boundary; muscularity, body composition, age, and clinical context all affect interpretation.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter weight, height.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How overweight is calculated

BMI=weight(kg)/height(m)². The BMI-25 comparison weight is 25×height(m)²; the difference is shown only when current weight is above that reference. This is a screening threshold for adults, not a health boundary; muscularity, body composition, age, and clinical context all affect interpretation. At 1.70 m, BMI 25 corresponds to 72.25 kg.

BMI=weight(kg)/height(m)²; adult comparison threshold 25.
A worked example

At 1.70 m, BMI 25 corresponds to 72.25 kg.

Assumptions & useful context

Adult BMI is a screening measure, not a diagnosis.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

CDC: Adult BMI categories and calculation ↗

Frequently asked questions

Does BMI above 25 mean I am unhealthy?

No. BMI is one screening measure and should be interpreted with other information.

Is the same cutoff used for children?

No. Children and teens use age- and sex-specific BMI percentiles.
